title: Patient Account Terms Schedule for the Testing Supplies Tiers
content:
These are the money terms the patient financial services team applies to a customer's balance on the Blood Glucose Testing Supply Program, by tier. Amounts are in USD.

| Tier | Payment plan: smallest balance | Payment plan: most monthly installments | Payment plan: smallest monthly installment | Past-due age, days after posting | Past-due amount that holds shipments | Small-balance write-off, largest balance | Hardship waiver allowed | Hardship income ceiling, percent of poverty guideline | Credit refund time limit, days |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Testing Supplies Self-Pay Program | 150.00 | 0 | 25.00 | 15 | 50.00 | 0.00 | No | 200 | 30 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial HMO Program | 150.00 | 6 | 25.00 | 90 | 75.00 | 4.99 | Yes | 200 | 30 |
| Testing Supplies Commercial PPO Program | 150.00 | 6 | 25.00 | 90 | 75.00 | 4.99 | Yes | 200 | 30 |
| Testing Supplies Medicare Advantage Program | 100.00 | 10 | 20.00 | 120 | 75.00 | 4.99 | Yes | 200 | 60 |
| Testing Supplies Original Medicare Program | 100.00 | 10 | 20.00 | 120 | 75.00 | 0.00 | Yes | 200 | 60 |
| Testing Supplies Medicaid Program | 100.00 | 0 | 20.00 | 0 | 75.00 | 0.00 | No | 200 | 60 |

**Column definitions**

- *Smallest balance* — the smallest patient balance for which an interest-free payment plan may be requested.
- *Most monthly installments* — the longest interest-free plan; 0 means payment plans are not offered on the tier.
- *Smallest monthly installment* — the smallest installment a plan accepts.
- *Past-due age* — the age in calendar days after its posting date at which an unpaid patient-balance posting becomes past due for the shipment hold test; 0 means shipments are never held for a past-due balance on the tier.
- *Past-due amount* — the past-due amount at or above which further shipments are held under the past-due rule.
- *Small-balance write-off* — the largest remaining balance written off as a small balance instead of being statemented; 0.00 means no small-balance write-off on the tier.
- *Hardship waiver allowed* — whether a documented financial-hardship waiver of patient cost share may be granted case by case.
- *Hardship income ceiling* — household income ceiling for a hardship waiver, as an integer percent of the current HHS federal poverty guideline for the household size.
- *Credit refund time limit* — calendar days, counted from the posting date of the entry that created the credit, within which a credit balance is refunded.

**Reading example (hypothetical balance).** A balance of 120.00 meets the 100.00 smallest balance of the Medicare tiers but not the 150.00 of the commercial tiers; on the self-pay and Medicaid tiers no plan exists at any balance, because their most monthly installments figure is 0.
